Finale application installations for macOS and Windows, Finale 1.0.0 through Finale 2011, rather than authored documents; deliverables in research/corpora/rpatters1-installs/. 4536 distinct source hashes across 12116 loose files, so this corpus is heavily duplicated across versions. This corpus now has exports and the semantic half of the pipeline runs: 3090 adjacent-exact companions, being 3066 Finale 2011 documents and the 24 WinFin 2.2 tutorial files. Re-surveyed 2026-08-12 after the Finale 2011 install DVD was imaged and its Mac and Windows payloads mined (count rose from 9764 to 12116). Finale 2011 is version 16.0.0.30, previously unverified in VERSION_MATRIX.md. Excluded: 'Finale PDK' (MakeMusic proprietary, outside this project's provenance boundary); '*.lib', '*.fan' and '*.fpa'; the Finale 2014.5/25/26/27 application bundles (MUSX-era only); and '*/Libraries*', which holds Finale's setting libraries rather than scores and contributed ~900 specimens no era framing classifies. KEEP='*Default*' re-admits the stock font-default files that live inside that excluded tree; the pattern is not '*Font Default*' because 'Handwritten Default' and 'Default Fonts' carry no such substring. Those files still classify under no epoch and recover nothing, which is a reader gap and the reason to keep them visible. inventory.py no longer falls back to a corpus-wide basename search: in a corpus of repeated installs the same filename recurs in every version directory by design, and the previous run's 7266 fallback-ambiguous and 112 fallback-unique pairings were all false, every one of them matching some other version's source to a Finale 2011 export.

Controlled fixtures committed to this repository, surveyed as a corpus in their own right; deliverables in research/corpora/tracked-evidence/. 179 loose *.mus files, 177 distinct by content and all 179 paired adjacent-exact with a Finale 27 companion, which is the highest companion coverage of any survey and the reason this cohort exists. Its unique contribution is the earliest era: both private corpora begin at Finale 1.8.7, so the only companion-backed Finale 1.0.0 evidence in any survey is the 39 fixtures here, along with the controlled one-variable edit pairs that no authored corpus can supply. Products present: 1.0.0 (39), 2.6 (23), 3.7 (18), 97 (10), 98 (3), 2000 (8), 2002 (11), 2003 (8), 2004b (6), 2005 (20), 2006 (6), 2007 (1), 2008 (4), 2011 (7), 2012 (15). Its companion convention is a '-finale27' directory holding '<stem>.musx', matching rpatters1-installs rather than rpatters1-main. Surveyed without --sniff-content and without archives: every source is named *.mus and committed loose. Unlike the other two surveys the corpus itself ships with the repository, so this row can be re-derived from a clone: run scripts/inventory.py against tests/evidence with the export convention above, which needs no private configuration. The conf that lets ./regenerate.sh drive it alongside the other two lives under the ignored private/ tree like theirs, and holds nothing private. It is tiny by design, so it settles questions about specific eras and must never be read as a percentage. Re-surveyed 2026-08-17 after twelve controlled lyric-options saves were added and the count rose from 69 to 81. The two Finale 2011 fixtures matter out of proportion to their number: **no other survey contains an authored Finale 2011 document at all**, and that release turned out to be where this class's edge-punctuation boundary falls. The installs corpus has 597 companion-backed Finale 2011 documents but they are Finale's own shipped sample content, converted into the release rather than created in it, so they do not show what a new document of that release writes. Several are the only specimen of something: F100-wext-push-6-lift-5.mus names the only two lyric values a Coda-banner document stores; F372-lyricopts-changed.mus is the only document anywhere that varies the hyphen separation; F2000-lyropts-align-just.mus is the only one in any survey that uses the legacy alignment value 3; and the three Finale 2011 auto-numbering saves are the only documents that carry those four fields set at all. F2012-lyric-punct.mus is the only specimen in any survey that carries a lyric punctuation ignore list: Finale writes the list as a variable-length tail on selector 57 and only when it differs from the stock set, so all 1,189 companion-backed documents of the reference corpus are silent on it and no corpus of any size could have located it. F2012-lyropts-noign-punct.mus is the only published document anywhere with the syllable edge-punctuation switch cleared, so it is the sole fixture exercising selector 57 word 4 set rather than clear. Re-surveyed 2026-08-18 after F2006-text-inserts.mus was added and the count rose from 81 to 82. That fixture is the only document in any survey that exercises Finale's text inserts deliberately, and it is the only one that can: Finale 2006 is the first release to write Enigma commands in the binary form and the last to export ETF, so it is the sole version where the same text block exists both encoded and spelled out. Its .mus, .etf and Finale 27 companion agree on all 21 records and together fix 25 of the binary command codes, the full 0-15 digit range, and the fact that an argument is a signed two's-complement value. It also settles that Finale 2006's File Info still has only four fields, so lyricist, arranger and subtitle arrived later. Re-surveyed again the same day after F2008-BE-text-inserts.mus was added and the count rose from 82 to 83. It is the only big-endian Finale 2008 document in any survey, PowerPC-authored because the Intel-era save crashed, and the only one anywhere that carries all seven File Info fields: by that release they have left the header for the text pool. It also carries the four inserts appended past the alphabetical run of command codes and the only one-digit argument, so between it and F2006-text-inserts.mus the two fixtures fix 30 of the codes and all three argument widths. Re-surveyed once more the same day after F2011-text-inserts.mus was added and the count rose from 83 to 84. It closes the binary Enigma command table: Finale 2009 introduced marking categories and Finale 2010 automatic rehearsal marks, so Finale 2011 is the earliest available release able to write ^fontTxt, ^fontMus, ^fontNum and ^rehearsal in one document, and with those four every command musxdom's EnigmaString.h documents has a located code. It also refuted the second and last prediction drawn from the shape of that table: the font-category commands are appended past the inserts at 0xa4-0xa6, not placed among the style commands at 0x80-0x83 where they would belong. Between it, F2006-text-inserts.mus and F2008-BE-text-inserts.mus, no fixture in this corpus reports a command code this reader cannot read. Re-surveyed 2026-08-18 a third time after five text fixtures were added and the count rose from 84 to 89. Four are Finale 1.0.0 and they open the Coda-banner epoch's text, which no document in any survey had previously contained at all: before them 26 tracked documents of that era were silent, so what looked like an undecoded framing was an absence of evidence. F100-short-text.mus and F100-long-text-w-insert.mus are a controlled pair differing in one block's text, which is what isolated the HT/HS record pair; F100-text-other-inserts.mus shows the insert character standing for three different inserts chosen by the style record; F100-lyric-text.mus is the only document of the era anywhere with lyrics. The fifth, F372-fileinfo-text.mus, settles the lower end of FileInfoText by the dialog rather than the bytes -- Finale 3.7.2 is the earliest available release whose dialog offers the fields -- and exposes a third text-pool framing between the Coda chunks and the Finale 97 records, in which a record has no terminator. All five carry an ETF export as well as a Finale 27 companion, so every reading has two independent witnesses. Re-surveyed 2026-08-18 a fourth time after two bookmark fixtures were added and the count rose from 89 to 91. F372-bookmarks.mus and F2012-bookmarks.mus are the same two bookmarks on either side of the Unicode boundary, the second being the first upgraded and re-saved. Together they show that bookmark text becomes an ordinary text-pool record at Finale 2012, keyword 'bookmark', and that its text is UTF-8: the guillemets and a u-umlaut are two bytes each there and one byte each in the earlier form, which keeps the text in a BK others family instead. Finale 3.7.2 is the earliest available release with bookmarks at all, so it bounds their arrival from above and says nothing more. The F2012 specimen is an edited artifact: the upgrade prepended mojibake to the bookmark text and it was removed by hand before saving. Re-surveyed 2026-08-18 a fifth time after F2002-fileinfo-text.mus was added and the count rose from 91 to 92. It settles that the FileInfoText header offsets still hold across the DCL epoch, so File Info moves into the text pool somewhere after Finale 2002 rather than at the epoch boundary. Unlike the other text fixtures it is an authored score rather than a purpose-built document, and its twelve block texts exercise the pool more widely than any of them: inserts appearing mid-sentence and inside parentheses, a block that changes size and style partway through, and a long paragraph with curly quotes and an italic run. Re-surveyed 2026-08-18 a sixth time after five smart-shape custom line fixtures were added and the count rose from 92 to 97. Two of the five are parents that carry no edit at all: F2000-empty.mus and F2002-empty.mus are untouched new documents authored in their own release under SheepShaver, kept there so that every later fixture from that virtual machine can be a one-variable diff against one of them. That was not possible before, because the Mass Copy and Note Spacing documents this corpus was built from cannot be moved into the classic-Mac guest. F2000-ssline-offsets.mus is the only document in any survey that fills every position and line-adjustment word of an `ls` record, each with a distinct value, which is what established words 19 through 33 and showed that Finale writes one vertical control into two of them. F2012-ssline-offsets.mus is its back-save and is the only pair anywhere stating the same six custom line styles on both sides of the Unicode boundary; it corrected the Finale 2012 character widening, which shifts only the Char parameter block and not a Dashed record's dash lengths. F2002-clef-stem-font.mus is the only document in any survey that points a clef, a stem connection and a text symbol insert at a text font rather than a music font, each beside a control still using the default music font; it established that a stored character is a byte in its own font's encoding rather than a code point, which no corpus of any size could have shown, because every clef, connection and insert in every other document uses a music font whose byte is already the right answer. Finale 2002 is the earliest available release whose clef dialog offers a font override at all, which is why that fixture is not a Finale 2000 document like the other four.
